title: Other Western religious orders: bounded missal and proper witnesses

traditions.label: Augustinian Hermits (OSA)
traditions.scope: Order-labelled Latin missal and Mass proper witnesses, distinct from Augustinian Canons Regular and Recollect translations.
traditions.coverage_note: The early printing has conflicting bibliographic and colophon years; the directly seen 1926 book is a proper of Mass and Office. Neither supplies a continuous OSA missal sequence.

traditions.label: Order of Mercy (Mercedarians)
traditions.scope: Mercedarian whole-missal bibliography and a separately approved Latin Mass proper.
traditions.coverage_note: The 1560 Barcelona missal is an incomplete surviving copy, while the 1976 approval concerns only a proper. Intervening witnesses and text are not collated.

traditions.label: Servite Order
traditions.scope: The medieval Servite-use manuscript and the two complementary 1972 Latin Mass-proper volumes.
traditions.coverage_note: The medieval codex is Roman Curia use for Servite friars. Its additions and the 1998 second typical edition need original-page review.

traditions.label: Order of the Most Holy Trinity (Trinitarians)
traditions.scope: Mixed medieval Mass-book witness, a catalogued printed missal, and an approved modern proper, with their different evidence classes preserved.
traditions.coverage_note: The manuscript Mass folios and 1529 printing remain uninspected; the 1975 official approval establishes a proper, not a complete missal.

traditions.label: Hospitaller Order of Saint John of Jerusalem, Rhodes and Malta
traditions.scope: A corrected 1553 printed-missal catalogue identity and the 1987 Latin proper with lectionary.
traditions.coverage_note: The owning BnF catalogue rejects the former 1551 date for its B-320 copy. The medieval local books and later 2005 proper remain without a checked original-text sequence.

sources.title: Missale Ordinis Fratrum Eremitarum Sancti Augustini de observantia, BSB 2 Inc.c.a. 2591
sources.inspection: The source inventory reports BSB canvas 565 directly inspected for its 1496 colophon and the opening's Roman Curia order; BSB manifest metadata identifies shelfmark, 256 leaves and conflicting 1491 catalogue date. These identified leaves are used only at that extent. Re-inspected 2026-10-22 (orders batch5): canvas 565 (fol. 270v) downloaded at 1600 px (SHA-256 7920b830…, 728,665 bytes) and the date line cropped and viewed. The printed colophon reads Anno salutis M.CCCC. lxxxxi with Pontifice maximo Innocentio; the red Arabic numerals 1496 after it are an added, non-typographic entry, not the printed date. GW M23973 and BSB-Ink M-441 (records read) date the edition 1491 (Nuremberg, types of Georg Stuchs).
sources.limitations: The red 1496 entry in this copy is unexplained (rubricator's or owner's addition); it does not date the printing. Only the colophon and catalogue identity are used; no scan or text is retained in this dossier.

sources.title: BAV Pal. lat. 500, Missale Romanum fratrum eremitarum sancti Augustini: DigiVatLib images
sources.inspection: Complete 387-canvas IIIF manifest acquired. Images of ff. 85r (canvas 175), 96v (canvas 199), 183v (canvas 373) and 184r (canvas 374) downloaded at 1600 px and viewed.
sources.limitations: Four folios only; no layer-wide collation, transcription or complete-book reading. Readings of the abbreviated colophon and rubric are visual, controlled by the holding-library description.

sources.title: Heidelberg Bibliotheca Palatina digital, codex description of Vatican Pal. lat. 500
sources.inspection: Whole description HTML fetched and read: dating, gathering structure, displaced gathering ff. 82–91, two Canon sections, colophon 183vb and dated addition 184rab.
sources.limitations: Catalogue palaeographic dates are estimates. The description itself doubts that the 1314 colophon date fits the hand of the final gatherings.

sources.title: Proprium missarum et Officiorum Ordinis Eremitarum Sancti Augustini (1926)
sources.inspection: Existing dated inventory review acquired the 252-page PDF and inspected PDF pp. 1–2: order title and Prior General publication formula, 5 August 1926 concordance certificate and separate 9 August Tournai imprimatur.
sources.limitations: Mass and Office proper, not a complete missal. Rights to the host's scan or transcription have not been affirmed for redistribution; only metadata and limited findings are recorded.

sources.title: Sacred Congregation for Divine Worship, OSA Latin and Spanish proper confirmations, Notitiae 11 (1975)
sources.inspection: Official journal printed p. 234 (PDF p. 32) rendered and viewed; text layer read. Reused prior-lane copy of the same issue, rehashed.
sources.limitations: A summary of decrees, not the decree text or the printed book. Publication of the confirmed Latin book is not dated by this entry.

sources.title: USUARIUM 8574, ACA Barcelona XXVI.1.1, Mercedarian missal (1560)
sources.inspection: Existing dated inventory review inspected the book metadata and contents table identifying the incomplete 1560 missal and a separately bound proper at images 579–609 dated 1641.
sources.limitations: Original title, body and missing final folios have not been seen; the 1641 supplement must not be dated 1560. USUARIUM page access requires approval and its dataset requests attribution.

sources.title: Sacred Congregation for Divine Worship, Mercedarian proper confirmation, Notitiae 14 (1978)
sources.inspection: Official journal entry inspected in the existing dated research packet at printed pp. 289–290: Latin Proprium Missarum confirmation dated 1 July 1976, protocol CD 268/76; 1976 publication distinguished from 1977 Italian and Spanish versions.
sources.limitations: Approval notice and publication statement only. The complete Latin proper, approval text and reception by individual houses are not acquired.

sources.title: BAV Pal. lat. 505, Missale Romanum ad usum fratrum Servorum Mariae
sources.inspection: Heidelberg manuscript description and BAV IIIF metadata reviewed in the existing dated inventory: southwestern German manuscript, second half of the fourteenth century; main missal ff. 1ra–321rb and later Mass additions ff. 321rb–322v. Two BAV images were acquired in that review.
sources.limitations: The original Mass folios and added formulary layer have not been read through. BAV images assert copyright; this dossier retains no image bytes.

sources.title: BAV Pal. lat. 505, Missale Romanum ad usum fratrum servorum Mariae: DigiVatLib images
sources.inspection: Complete 662-canvas IIIF manifest acquired (the earlier recorded gap of missing canvases no longer applies to this delivery). Images of f. 1r (canvas 5) and f. 321r (canvas 647) downloaded at 1400 px and viewed; f. 321v (canvas 648) downloaded but not read.
sources.limitations: Two folios read; no complete Mass collation. The erasure under the Servite rubric reported by Salmon is cited from the holding-library description, not independently confirmed from the image.

sources.title: Sacred Congregation for Divine Worship, Servite calendar and Mass proper confirmations, Notitiae 9 (1973)
sources.inspection: Official entry inspected in the existing dated inventory at printed pp. 284–286/PDF pp. 41–43: 6 February 1971 calendar confirmation and 1 October 1971 Mass proper approval are separate acts.
sources.limitations: The act summary does not provide the complete proper text, establish dates of house use or prove a whole-missal recension.

sources.title: Notitiae 11 (1975), bibliography of the 1972 Servite Proprium Missarum
sources.inspection: Official journal bibliography inspected in existing dated inventory: Rome 1972, volume I Antiphonale Sacramentarium and volume II Lectionarium.
sources.limitations: Original volumes, full contents and precise relationship between the 1971 decree and printed editions remain uncollated.

sources.title: USUARIUM 2548 and ARCA Provins Impr. XVI a 8, Trinitarian missal (1529)
sources.inspection: The existing dated inventory checked USUARIUM title, 1529 print metadata and contents index through colophon p. 551; ARCA identifies the same Provins copy as 272 folios with 279 digital views.
sources.limitations: Both catalogues may depend on one copy. Original title, colophon and Mass text were not available; the catalogue year is not evidence of a reform or reception.

sources.title: Provins, Bibliothèque patrimoniale, Impr. XVI a 8: IRHT/ARCA page images of the 1529 Trinitarian missal
sources.inspection: Prior-lane IRHT IIIF downloads (17 October 2026) rehashed and viewed on 21 October: canvas 4 (f. 1r title), canvas 5 (f. 2r January calendar, extracted from a partial ZIP), canvas 143 (f. 140r Preparatio ante missam), canvas 148 (ff. 144v–145r Marian preface and Canon Te igitur to Hanc igitur), canvases 275–276 (Commune prosarum to fo. lx and final 'Trinitati laus perhennis').
sources.limitations: Seven openings of 279 views. The IRHT image host timed out on 21 October, so no fresh download. No dated colophon was found on the title or final prose leaves inspected; the 1529 year and Paris printer Nicolaus Prevost remain catalogue statements.

sources.title: Sacred Congregation for Divine Worship, Trinitarian proper confirmations, Notitiae 11 (1975)
sources.inspection: Official journal printed p. 343/PDF p. 60 inspected in dated regional permission review: Latin Mass and Hours proper confirmed 18 October 1975, protocol CD 172/75; Vincent Grossi Mass recorded separately 27 October, protocol CD 400/75.
sources.limitations: An approval summary, not the complete proper or a whole Trinitarian missal. Individual-house use and earlier proper comparison remain unestablished.

sources.title: BnF catalogue cb36827961c, Hospitaller missal B-320 (Lyon, 1553)
sources.inspection: Owning BnF catalogue checked in the dated Hospitaller review: title, 1553 Lyon heirs of Jacques Giunta imprint, B-320 item, [22]-CCCLXXIIII leaves and explicit correction of B-320's former 1551 date.
sources.limitations: No original folio inspected. A 1551 edition remains unproved, and other catalogue routes may describe another copy; no revised text or reprint relation is inferred.

sources.title: Sacred Congregation for Divine Worship, Hospitaller proper confirmation, Notitiae 23 (1987)
sources.inspection: Official journal printed p. 1038/PDF p. 34 inspected in dated Hospitaller review: 4 July 1987 Latin Proprium Missarum confirmation, protocol 839/87. DLI record 19078 separately identifies the 1987 Latin editio typica with lectionary, Rome, 136 pages.
sources.limitations: The notice names the Mass proper, not expressly the companion lectionary's approval extent. The original book and complete text are unacquired; scan or modern editorial rights are unresolved.

sources.title: OCSO, Liturgy: Missal and Cistercian proper
sources.inspection: Order page directly read on 2026-10-20, Missal paragraph: prayers for Mass and Divine Office proper of Cistercian calendar approved for use in 1983, with later saints added. History and Calendar paragraphs distinguish older shared Cistercian liturgy and postconciliar variations.
sources.limitations: The page does not identify a dated original decree, first Latin printing, precise text or every subsequent addition. It supplies no complete OCSO missal independent of the Roman base. The exact bounded continuation in ocso-next independently records OCSO 1975 and OCist 1977 confirmations plus a 1983 publication; this retrospective's general 1983 approval remains a discrepancy requiring its original instrument. The empty OCSO tradition and superseded gap have moved to that dossier.

sources.title: OCSO, General Norms for the Liturgy of the Order
sources.inspection: The dated regional-permissions review inspected sections I.B, III.A.1 and III.D, PDF pp. 1–2, 11–12 and 15: the Roman Missal base, four listed Cistercian ceremonial customs, monastery calendar and bounded regional prayer options. It cites the Roman reply of 8 June 1971, protocol 525/70.
sources.limitations: The original 1971 Roman reply, exact regional approvals and actual monastery choices have not been inspected. Operative norms are not a separate whole-missal edition.

stages.label: OSA observance missal printed at Nuremberg, 1491
stages.date_label: 1491 printed colophon (M.CCCC. lxxxxi, under Pope Innocent VIII); a red 1496 is added in the BSB copy
stages.scope: Order-labelled Latin whole missal in Roman Curia order; title and colophon evidence only.
stages.witness_label: BSB 2 Inc.c.a. 2591, Missale Ordinis Fratrum Eremitarum Sancti Augustini de observantia
stages.summary: An Augustinian Hermits observance missal printed for the order at the command of vicar general Andreas Proles; its printed colophon dates it 1491, and the 1496 previously read there is a later red addition in this copy.

evidence.locus: BSB IIIF canvas 565 (fol. 270v), colophon; GW M23973; BSB-Ink M-441
evidence.claim: The printed dating formula is Anno salutis M.CCCC. lxxxxi under Pope Innocent; the red Arabic 1496 following it is not typeset. Both incunable catalogues give 1491.

stages.limitations: The former 1491/1496 conflict was a misreading of an added red numeral; the coordinate now follows the printed colophon. Title, opening and colophon do not establish an independent rite or textual relation to Roman and later OSA books.
stages.reception: An intended order-use title, without a named house's adoption record.

stages.label: Pal. lat. 500: early fourteenth-century Augustinian Hermit missal core
stages.date_label: First half of the fourteenth century (catalogue); colophon at 183vb reads 1314, on St Ulrich's day, but stands in later-added gatherings
stages.scope: Main manuscript ff. 1ra–81vb and 92ra–173vb with its own Canon at 96va–99ra; excludes the inserted ff. 82–91 and the added final gatherings.
stages.summary: An order missal of the Augustinian Hermits. Its older Canon at f. 96v has red rubrics within the Te igitur for bowing, kissing the altar and the threefold sign over host and chalice. The colophon at 183vb, in the later-added final gatherings, names Brother H. of the Hermits of St Augustine; whether it refers to the scribe of this core is unestablished.

evidence.claim: Dates the core hands early in the fourteenth century, distinguishes the inserted Canon gathering and the added final gatherings, and doubts that the 1314 colophon dates the last gatherings.

Te igitur of the older Canon with interlinear red rubrics for inclining, kissing the altar and signing three times over host and chalice; Memento includes 'pro quibus tibi offerimus vel qui tibi offerunt'.
Black colophon dated anno domini 1314 on St Ulrich's day; red colophon names Brother H. of the Hermits of the order of St Augustine.

stages.limitations: Copying-date bounds are a catalogue estimate, not years of use. Because the colophon stands in later gatherings, 1314 may be copied from an exemplar or miswritten; it is not used as the stage date. No complete collation.
stages.reception: Order-labelled book of German provenance; no general chapter adoption or house-wide use is established.

stages.label: Pal. lat. 500: inserted Canon gathering, about 1400
stages.date_label: About 1400, catalogue script date for ff. 85ra–88rb
stages.scope: The displaced gathering ff. 82–91, with a Canon in textura formata at 85ra–88rb.
stages.witness_label: BAV Pal. lat. 500, layer attributed to about 1400
stages.summary: A second, more formal Canon was inserted into the codex. Its Te igitur page at f. 85r carries red crosses but none of the interlinear bowing and altar-kiss rubrics written in the older Canon at f. 96v.

evidence.claim: Identifies ff. 82–91 as an inserted unit and dates its Canon script about 1400.
Te igitur through the opening of Communicantes, with crosses in red but no interlinear gesture rubrics on this page.

stages.limitations: One page of each Canon compared. Whether the inserted Canon replaced the older one in use, and why it was added, is unestablished; no transition is drawn.
stages.reception: Insertion into an order book shows later use of this codex, not order-wide change.

stages.label: Pal. lat. 500: Mass of the Fourteen Holy Helpers added in 1466
stages.date_label: 1466, year written in the addition's own rubric at 184r
stages.witness_label: BAV Pal. lat. 500, layer attributed to 1466
stages.summary: The rubric introduces a Mass of the fourteen helpers to be said in any tribulation and carries the year 1466. Its collect, secret and postcommunion name George, Blaise, Erasmus, Pantaleon, Vitus, Christopher, Denis, Cyriac, Achatius, Eustace, Giles, Magnus, Margaret, Barbara and Catherine — fifteen names under the fourteen-helpers heading.

evidence.claim: Rubric 'Sequitur missa de xiv adiutoribus pro quacumque tribulatione dicenda 1466' with the Mass formulary in two columns.
Accepts 1466 as the date of entry; two further additions at 184va–185ra follow later.

stages.limitations: A dated addition in one codex. It does not show that the Mass was absent from other OSA books or adopted by the order.
stages.reception: Attests use of this codex in 1466; the house is not identified here.

stages.label: 1926 OSA Mass and Office proper
stages.scope: Order proper for Mass and Office, not a whole missal.
stages.witness_label: Proprium missarum et Officiorum Ordinis Eremitarum Sancti Augustini, 1926
stages.summary: The printed title names a Prior General's order, and the following leaf certifies agreement with an approved original. Neither leaf dates a new textual revision.

evidence.locus: PDF pp. 1–2, title, 5 August certificate and 9 August imprimatur
evidence.claim: The 1926 publication is an OSA Mass and Office proper with an edition-concordance certificate.

stages.limitations: Mass contents and relation to the 1674, 1715, 1965 and 2006 proper leads remain uncollated; no transition is drawn.
stages.reception: The order edition formula indicates intended use, not a census of local implementation.

stages.label: 1975 OSA Latin Mass and Hours proper confirmation
stages.date_label: 15 April 1975 Latin confirmation (Prot. n. 2435/74); Spanish confirmed 17 May 1975 (Prot. n. 588/75)
stages.scope: The order's postconciliar Latin proper texts of Masses and Liturgy of the Hours, as confirmed; not a printed book.
stages.witness_label: Acts only: Notitiae 11 (1975) p. 234; the Spanish-proper candidate western:additional-orders-osa-first-postconciliar (1975 Spanish confirmation, 1976 Rome missal reported) is related but not linked.
stages.summary: The Congregation confirmed the OSA proper Mass and Hours texts in Latin on 15 April 1975 and their Spanish version on 17 May. On 15 May the Augustinian Recollects were allowed to use the texts already confirmed for the OSA.

evidence.claim: Ordo Fratrum Sancti Augustini, 15 apr. 1975 (Prot. n. 2435/74): Latin proper texts of Masses and Liturgy of the Hours confirmed; 17 May 1975 (Prot. n. 588/75) Spanish version; Augustinian Recollects 15 May 1975 (Prot. n. 582/75) permitted to use them.

stages.limitations: This resolves the existence and date of a Latin original only at the level of the confirmation notice. The Latin book, its publication and its contents are not inspected; the 1976 Rome missal remains a report.
stages.reception: Confirmation for the order; house use and Recollect adoption in practice are not documented.

stages.label: 1560 Mercedarian whole-missal witness
stages.scope: The surviving ACA Barcelona missal, missing its last folios; the later bound proper is excluded.
stages.witness_label: Missale secundum consuetudinem Ordinis de Mercede, ACA XXVI.1.1
stages.summary: The catalogue identifies a 1560 order-use missal and separately lists a 1641 proper booklet bound with it.

evidence.locus: USUARIUM book 8574 metadata and contents images 579–609
evidence.claim: The 1560 missal and 1641 bound proper are distinct bibliographic objects.

stages.limitations: Original leaves and missing extent uninspected; no specific prayer or rubric can be attributed to this printing from the catalogue alone.
stages.reception: The title claims order use; no house reception is checked.

stages.label: 1976 Latin Mercedarian Mass proper
stages.witness_label: Proprium Missarum Ordinis Beatae Mariae Virginis de Mercede
stages.summary: The Holy See confirmed the Latin Mass proper under CD 268/76; later vernacular approvals are separate events.

evidence.claim: The notice names the Latin proper, confirmation date and publication year.

stages.limitations: The original 1976 volume is not acquired. The approval cannot turn the 1560 whole missal into its direct predecessor.
stages.reception: Order-wide confirmation is recorded; use of a particular printing at any house is unverified.

stages.label: Medieval Roman-Curia missal for Servite friars
stages.date_label: Second half of the fourteenth century, manuscript catalogue estimate
stages.scope: Main manuscript ff. 1ra–321rb, excluding later added Mass formularies.
stages.summary: The holding-library description identifies a Servite-use missal with Roman Curia usage, distinct from its later additions.

evidence.locus: Heidelberg codex description, title, date and ff. 1ra–322v contents
evidence.claim: The main Missal and later Mass additions occupy distinguishable folio ranges.

Opening rubric 'Incipit ordo missalis fratrum servorum sancte Marie secundum consuetudinem Romane curie', First Sunday of Advent station at St Mary Major, with a rubric adding a daily collect of St Mary.

stages.limitations: Catalogue-estimated copying bounds, not years of use. The original Mass text is uncollated, and the later additions are not separately dated. The opening rubric was read from the image on 2026-10-21; the reported erasure beneath its Servite wording is the catalogue's observation.
stages.reception: A codex described for Servite friars; no general chapter or house adoption is established.

stages.label: 1972 Servite Mass proper, sacramentary and lectionary
stages.scope: Complementary volumes I Antiphonale Sacramentarium and II Lectionarium, one proper book set rather than two recensions.
stages.witness_label: Proprium Missarum Ordinis Servorum Mariae, Rome 1972, volumes I–II
stages.summary: The 1971 Mass-proper approval and official bibliography establish a 1972 two-volume Servite proper set; the separate calendar confirmation was 6 February 1971.

evidence.claim: The calendar and Mass-proper confirmations have distinct 1971 dates.
The 1972 proper has two named complementary volumes.

stages.limitations: Original volumes and their complete text are uninspected. The 1998 editio typica altera is bibliographically identified but cannot yet supply a checked substantive transition.
stages.reception: The approval names the order proper; actual local use and particular copies are not evidenced.

stages.label: Pal. lat. 505: later added Mass formularies
stages.date_label: Later than the main hand; undated (several later textura hands and a fifteenth-century bastarda)
stages.witness_label: BAV Pal. lat. 505, additional Mass formularies
stages.summary: After the main hand ends the Palm Sunday procession at 321rb, another hand adds a Mass for the ruler: collect Deus temporalis vitae administrator, secret Deus qui subiectas tibi glorificas potestates and complenda Fidelem famulum tuum principem nostrum.

evidence.claim: Main-hand rubrics for the Palm Sunday procession end with Gloria laus; below, a smaller later hand writes the three prayers of a Mass for the prince.
Assigns 321rb–322v to several later hands, including a fifteenth-century bastarda.

stages.limitations: Undated and unpositioned. Only the first added formulary was read; the remaining additions at 321v–322v are uncollated.
stages.reception: Local additions in one Servite-house codex, probably Germersheim; not an order revision.

stages.label: 1529 printed Trinitarian missal witness
stages.scope: Provins Impr. XVI a 8, a standalone printed order missal; title, January calendar, Preparatio, Canon opening and final prose leaves inspected in images.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum fratrum Ordinis Sanctae Trinitatis de Redemptione Captivorum
stages.summary: USUARIUM and ARCA identify one 1529 Provins copy; the metadata is a book identity, not a reform date. The title page names the use of the friars of the Holy Trinity for the redemption of captives. The calendar keeps 28 January, St Agnes secundo, as totum duplex because of the order's foundation, and lists William of Bourges on 10 January.

evidence.locus: USUARIUM book 2548 title and contents index; ARCA Provins Impr. XVI a 8 object metadata
evidence.claim: The catalogues identify a 1529 printed Trinitarian missal in the Provins collection.
Title 'Missale ad usum fratrum ordinis sancte Trinitatis de redemptione captivorum' above a Man of Sorrows woodcut; no date or imprint on this page.
28 January 'Agnetis ij. Toti dup. propter ordi. inventionem'; 10 January Guillermi bituricensis archiepiscopi, nine lessons.
Preparatio ante missam with vesting prayers; Canon from Te igitur to Hanc igitur, with 'pro quibus tibi offerimus vel qui tibi offerunt' in the Memento.
The prose section ends 'Trinitati laus perhennis' without a dated colophon on these leaves.

stages.limitations: Seven openings inspected; completeness and text unverified. The 1529 date and Paris imprint remain catalogue statements because no dated colophon was found on the leaves read. BnF Latin 1022 is a mixed Office/Mass manuscript with later use layers, not an established ancestor.
stages.reception: Printed title states intended order use; actual distribution and celebration remain unverified.

stages.label: 1975 Trinitarian Latin Mass and Hours proper confirmation
stages.date_label: 18 and 27 October 1975 (Prot. CD 172/75; CD 400/75), covering the proper and the Mass of Blessed Vincent Grossi; the notice does not assign each date and protocol
stages.scope: The order's Latin proper of Masses and Liturgy of the Hours as confirmed; not a printed edition or whole missal.
stages.witness_label: Proprium Missarum et Liturgiae Horarum Ordinis SS.mae Trinitatis, Latin texts confirmed 1975
stages.summary: The Congregation confirmed the Latin text of the order's proper of Masses and Hours, together with the Mass of Blessed Vincent Grossi.

evidence.locus: Notitiae 11 (1975), printed p. 343 (PDF p. 61), section II
evidence.claim: Ordo Sanctissimae Trinitatis, 18 and 27 Oct. 1975 (Prot. CD 172/75; CD 400/75): Latin text of the order's proper of Masses and Hours and of the Mass of Blessed Vincent Grossi confirmed. Page image viewed 2026-10-21.

stages.limitations: The order-issued book, its publication year and its contents are not inspected. No descent from the 1529 missal is asserted.
stages.reception: Approval for the order; house use is not documented.

stages.label: 1553 Lyon Hospitaller missal witness
stages.scope: BnF B-320 copy's printed missal identity, without its uninspected Mass text or an invented 1551 predecessor.
stages.witness_label: BnF B-320, Lyon heirs of Jacques Giunta, 1553
stages.summary: The owning catalogue identifies the 1553 copy and explicitly corrects B-320's old 1551 misdate.

evidence.locus: BnF cb36827961c, publication, material description, Note(s) and B-320 item
evidence.claim: B-320 belongs to the 1553 Lyon printing, not a separately attested 1551 edition.

stages.limitations: Original leaves, order-specific text and relation to local Hospitaller manuscripts or other Lyon copies remain unexamined.
stages.reception: A printed order-use book, without house-level adoption evidence.

stages.label: 1987 Hospitaller Latin Mass proper with lectionary
stages.scope: Latin Proprium Missarum; its bibliographically joined Lectionarium is a complementary volume section, not a whole missal.
stages.witness_label: Proprium Missarum una cum Lectionario Ordinis Sancti Ioannis Hierosolymitani, Rome 1987
stages.summary: Notitiae records the Latin Mass-proper confirmation; the liturgical institute catalogue identifies the printed 136-page edition with lectionary.

evidence.claim: The approval is for the Latin Mass proper; a 1987 printed edition bears a lectionary in its title.

stages.limitations: Approval extent for the lectionary is not established by the notice; the complete 1987 book and 2005 second edition are uninspected.
stages.reception: Official approval and order bibliography establish intended order use, not a count of houses that used the printing.

gaps.missing: Collate Pal. lat. 500 layers beyond the four inspected folios; intervening OSA books and proper texts (1674, 1715, 1926 body, 1965); the printed Latin book behind the 15 April 1975 confirmation; original 2006 Latin approval. Narrowed 2026-10-22: the 1491/1496 conflict is resolved: the BSB incunable's printed colophon (canvas 565) reads 1491 under Pope Innocent, and the red 1496 beside it is an added, non-typographic entry; GW M23973 agrees. The OSA calendar confirmation of 18 October 1971 (Prot. n. 1763/71, Notitiae 8 (1972) p. 11, OCR text) and the 15 November 1974 calendar listing (Prot. n. 2329/74, Notitiae 11 (1975) p. 42, image) are separate component events.
gaps.next_source: Remaining Pal. lat. 500 folios (Canons 85ra–88rb and 96va–99ra in full, additions 184va–185ra); 1674/1715/1926/1965 source books; the 1975 Latin proper volume or the 1976 Rome missal; Acta OAR 2007 with the 2006 Latin proper.
gaps.consequence: Pal. lat. 500 core, inserted Canon and 1466 addition are separate dated attestations, and the 1975 Latin confirmation is documented; no early-to-modern OSA revision, text inheritance or continuous use is asserted.

gaps.missing: Original 1507/1560 books, 1617 and 1641 proper booklets, and 1694 printing need separation and text comparison.
gaps.next_source: ACA XXVI.1.1 original leaves and copy census; Madrid 1617 Royal Press copy; 1976 Latin proper and decree. 2026-10-22: Notitiae 9 (1973) p. 260 (OCR text) records the order's proper calendar confirmed 6 June 1973 (Prot. n. 882/73) and p. 256 a Latin profession rite (30 May 1973); no early-book information.
gaps.consequence: The 1976 proper cannot be presented as a whole-missal replacement or descendant of a particular early print.

gaps.missing: Pal. lat. 505 Mass text beyond f. 1r and the additions after the first formulary at 321rb, the 1745 bound proper and original 1972/1998 volumes remain uncollated.
gaps.next_source: Remaining BAV Pal. lat. 505 folios (complete manifest now delivered), OSZK RK 182(3) and official Servite Libri Liturgici OSM 1–2 and 1–2 bis front matter and component texts. Notitiae annual issues 1976–2010 gave no 1998 confirmation entry (bounded search).
gaps.consequence: No direct medieval-to-modern descent or 1972-to-1998 substantive revision edge is drawn.
